significance.justification: If verified true, the claim would license the form-(ii) causal conclusion that a "consistent low-rank direction across semantically-unrelated batches" carries subliminal traits and that removing its activation-gradient component suppresses transfer while preserving semantic distillation. This establishes both a phenomenon—a selective training-time defense—and a mechanism separating covert steering from useful learning, but it remains the standard separable-direction/causal-role/repair shape bounded to subliminal trait transfer rather than a law predicting other behaviors; Cloud et al.'s "Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data" makes that selective separation consequential because semantic filtering does not reliably remove the transmission. A verified-false result would informatively rule out consistent low-rank gradient orthogonalization as a generally selective account or defense, and true versus false are distinguishable through the asserted joint outcome of reduced transfer and preserved intended signal. Topic substitution would not retain this score: merely proposing to extend subliminal-learning research lacks the claim-specific causal separation, though the bounded single-behavior form keeps it only modestly above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "gradient-orthogonalization procedure" that extracts and removes an anomalously consistent low-rank activation-gradient direction; it is ex ante because it operates "during fine-tuning," before a subliminally influenced student is deployed. Its conclusion could be used by distillation practitioners as a trait-agnostic training-time safeguard and diagnostic across semantically unrelated data and unknown traits, rather than solely by researchers explaining an already observed failure. However, after moving to a new model the direction must be re-extracted, and the claim supplies a procedure for finding it rather than a transferable scaling law, threshold, or quantitative prediction about what the new model will contain. Topic substitution would lose both the proactive handle and its action window, so the reach comes from this claim rather than from the general importance of subliminal learning.
